# Open Questions for Brightline Cabinetry LLC — March 2026 close

Please answer inline or by reply email. Each item shows what happens to the
books when we get the answer.

1. **Unidentified mobile deposit, $4,312.00 (3/21).** The bank statement
   shows it with the bare memo "MOBILE DEPOSIT"; the payer is not named and
   no invoice matches the amount. Who paid it and what was it for? It
   currently sits in Other Current Liabilities / suspense (account 2100,
   AJE-2). If it turns out to be a customer payment, we'll apply it to their
   invoice and clear the liability. If it's a loan or the owner's money
   coming back in, it needs its own account instead.

2. **$1,500.00 transfer in on 3/14 from account "*4420".** Same treatment:
   currently parked in suspense (AJE-4 moved it out of Sales 4000 because we
   can't record revenue we can't support). Whose account is *4420 and what
   is this money for?

3. **Uchi restaurant, $212.00, 3/15 — "4 guests, Saturday 8:40pm"** per the
   card statement note. Is this a business meal or a personal charge? We
   have temporarily classified it as an owner's draw (AJE-7), which keeps it
   off company meal expense and off the 50%-deductible meal category. If the
   four were customers or subcontractors on a legitimate business purpose,
   tell us who and why, and we'll move it back to meals with a
   business-purpose note.

4. **Cascade CH-7731 was keyed twice; we reversed one copy.** Both copies of
   invoice CH-7731 ($4,860.00, dated 2/24/26) were booked — the emailed copy
   on 2/26/26 and the paper copy on 3/9/26 — and check #2040 paid the bill
   once (cleared 3/22). AJE-1 reverses the 3/9 paper-copy booking. Please
   confirm whether the **2/26 email-copy booking was already inside the
   closed February trial balance** (February A/P shows $27,615.40, and we
   have no February vendor-level detail to tell from). If it was, a second
   reversal of $4,860.00 is required (A/P drops to $29,505.40, materials
   expense drops $4,860.00); if it was not, AJE-1 is complete.

5. **Accounts receivable detail.** The books show $115,288.00 of
   receivables; the March 31 aging lists only $56,100.00 — a $59,188.00 gap.
   The aging's oldest item is 12/18/25, so older open invoices appear not to
   have rolled into it. Please send a customer-by-customer detail that
   agrees to the books, with any open quotes/retainers and any unbilled or
   unposted work identified.

6. **Accounts payable detail.** Payables on the books are $34,365.40. We can
   trace only $6,750.00 to March bill entries in the ledger (Rivera Finish
   Carpentry $5,600.00 + Allied Insurance $1,150.00), and even those lack
   the vendor's own invoice. The remaining $27,615.40 carries over from
   February with no supporting document at all. Please send a vendor-level
   A/P listing at 3/31 and the underlying invoices.

7. **Hardaway Builders, disputed invoice INV-1167, $9,800.00 (90+ days).**
   The aging footnote records the customer's warped-door claim and the
   owner's "we'll eat half," but no credit memo exists. We cannot book a
   write-down without a signed credit memo or the customer's written
   agreement (close policy: no adjustment without documentation). Please get
   that signed — it should take a day, not delay the close. If some of the
   disputed work was never billed, send the invoice or confirm it should not
   be billed.

8. **Prepaid insurance schedule.** The books carried $2,400.00 of prepaid at
   February 28 that we can't trace to any policy, and no amortization has
   run. What policy is it, what period does it cover, and when should it run
   through expense? (The new Allied Q2 bill of $1,150.00 is deferred in full
   to April–June per AJE-6 — confirm the binder dates so we can be sure no
   March days are covered.)

9. **Fixed assets.** Is there a depreciation schedule or fixed-asset list?
   The books show $148,000.00 of equipment against $61,250.00 accumulated
   depreciation, but no depreciation expense for 2026 to date. We recorded
   none for March for lack of a schedule and placed-in-service dates; if you
   send the list we'll compute it, including a January–March catch-up.

10. **Sales tax.** The books carry a $4,121.55 liability with no March
    activity and no filings in the file set. In which states does Brightline
    collect and remit sales tax, which period is next due, and is the
    $4,121.55 the amount still owed? We did not accrue March tax because we
    have no data on taxable vs. non-taxable billings.

11. **Shop lease.** March rent ($4,500.00) was billed 3/1 and paid 3/7
    (check #2036, cleared 3/9), so nothing is open — but there is no lease
    in the document set. Please send the lease (or confirm monthly amount,
    term, and any escalations) so we can validate the run-rate each month.

12. **Cash presentation and overdrafts.** At 2/28 the account was overdrawn
    $7,013.13; the GL and the bank's March starting balance agree, but
    management reports should label the negative balance clearly — tell us
    your preferred presentation. Also, the account was negative again 3/5–3/9
    (low point $5,501.35 overdrawn) and on 3/15 ($4,719.55): no NSF or
    overdraft fees appear on these statements — did any hit a second account
    or the card?

13. **Duplicate-purchase controls.** This month the Cascade bill arrived by
    email and by mail and was keyed twice. We can add a simple "vendor +
    invoice number" check at data-entry; want us to set that up for April?

facts.answer: That's from my personal checking, I moved money over to cover payroll. It's my money, not a sale.
Huh. I don't remember depositing anything that day. Maybe Carla (office) did? Let me ask her... (later) she doesn't know either. Can you just park it somewhere for now?
Cascade emails invoices and then mails a paper copy a couple of weeks later. Same invoice. We paid it once.
Uchi was my anniversary dinner, I grabbed the wrong card. Put it on me.
Still arguing with them. Don't write it off yet.
